refined_why: A's queue sits in three aligned columns (title, artist, time) under a clear wordmark/tab header with a calm progress rule; B runs each artist inline after its title, so the second column is ragged, and its dotted progress track looks unfinished.
brand_why: A's copy carries the deadpan wink ('now spoofing', the italic 'a power ballad about a fine, sung with the gravity it deserves'); B's all-lowercase names are deadpan too, but nothing on the screen is as cheeky as A's liner.

refined_why: A is one clean table with a two-line header and generous columns. B says '1 firing' twice (top right and the kiln rule) and truncates branches ('feat/glaze-retr…', 'dependabot/go_m…') while leaving unused width on the right.
brand_why: B's live kiln strip (step pips, 'firing 57s', and the per-row step lane with × where it broke) reads as a hot, workmanlike shop floor. A is the kit's run table with an orange 'firing' tag.

refined_why: B has quiet uppercase headers, dot ratings, a subtle selection bar and the detail below the list with breathing room. A's solid orange selection bar is heavy, it truncates ('The Grand Wolfhound Ass…', 'party of 4, …'), and it packs three regions into the frame.
brand_why: A's shaggy fringe in the header and the 'From past parties' quotes ('Not one hair on the character sheets') feel warm and adventurous. B's tidy table and '£96 × 2 nights £192' line lean toward a booking listing.

refined_why: B is composed: a banner for the selection, a table that fills the width, record-progress bars and keycap footer. A's pixel sprite is clipped against the top edge, and a third of the frame sits empty below the list.
brand_why: B is more generous and showy: spaced 'S T A R  B A L L O O N' marquee, lime bars to the record, 'yours' callout. A has a mascot sprite but otherwise reads as a plain score table.

refined_why: A highlights the matched 'night' in each title, keeps two-line rows aligned and docks a mini-player above the footer. B truncates the selected title ('replacement s…') with space left in the band column, and its blue 'cover' tag brings in a hue that appears nowhere else.
brand_why: B's voice is drier and cheekier ('2 covers nobody asked for', the liner 'waits for a bus that is not coming, for four minutes and twelve seconds'). A's 'sends up …' subtitles are the same joke repeated on every row.

refined_why: A has a spacious two-pane layout with the log in a tinted panel and × marks in a gutter. B crams the headline against the steps with no gap, says 'failed' in red four or five times (header, title, step, several log lines), and adds line numbers that crowd the log.
brand_why: Both are terse and workmanlike in bisque's red and orange. B's run metadata and '1040°C' content feel more of the shop, and A's quieter frame is more terse, so they even out.

refined_why: A's wording is clear, but it shows two competing focus cues (an orange bar beside Pay and a green fill on Keep looking) and the green is off-palette. B is tidy with a receipt rule, but it focuses the irreversible 'Book & pay' by default and its footer repeats 'book & pay' twice.
brand_why: B's 'Check the scroll before you roll.', '5 adventurers, dogs welcome' and 'Not yet' carry the adventurous voice. A's 'Party — Review — Payment' stepper and 'Pay $184 and book' read closer to a booking form, even with the fringe header.

refined_why: A is clean: one progress rule to the next rank, a single highlighted YOU row and well-aligned controls (only the sprite is clipped at the top). B repeats a loud lime 'YOU' chip three times down the score table, which turns the table into noise.
brand_why: B is more generous and showy: a marquee band, dates on every score, 'top 10 of 214', and 'You hold 2ND, 5TH and 9TH' bragging. A is restrained by comparison.

refined_why: In light, A's selected row is dark-brown text on a dark amber fill with weak contrast, and its faint rules nearly vanish. B's light set keeps a soft selection tint, a crisp left bar and readable dot ratings.
brand_why: As in the dark render, A's fringe header and past-party quotes carry warm and shaggy. B is a neat but generic listing.

refined_why: A uses the large room: a banner, a wide table with plays and last-played, and two lower panels (records lately, your night), though one name truncates. B's right pane is empty below its top three, the sprite is clipped at the top again, and the two-line rows halve the list's density.
brand_why: A is the more generous and showy floor: a marquee with sprite, lime record bars, a records feed and a 'your night' recap. B is calmer and reads as a catalogue.
